name: Spain
notes: Depth: seed. Scope: national level. R001 (2026-10-21) read the Congreso roll call of 7 Jun 2022 on the Unidas Podemos wealth-tax bill (58 yes votes), the BOE text of Ley 38/2022 that created the solidarity tax on large fortunes, press reports of Sumar's 2023 programme, statements by Sánchez, Montero, Bustinduy and two former prime ministers, Oxfam Intermon's 2026 report, Gestha, UGT and CCOO. Register: root, Cortes Generales, the 19 autonomous communities and cities (ISO 3166-2:ES) the 52 provinces and the 8,132 municipios (INE list of 1 Jan 2026, the map tier). Party for the deputies comes from Wikidata (three left blank). Not done: final Congreso and Senate votes on Ley 38/2022 and the Jan 2024 extension, XV-legislature bills, party programmes beyond Sumar, economists, media, wealthy individuals, regional parliaments and local bodies. Only Spanish and English were searched. R002 (2026-10-21) added the PSOE and six other parties, the 2022 expert committee and its chair, the Generalitat and Parlament of Catalonia (Decree-law 10/2024), Zucman, a Vigo mayor, and re-graded the Club de Madrid letter against the primary text. The Congreso blocked the scanner (HTTP 403) mid-run, so no XV-legislature votes were read. R003 added Economistas Frente a la Crisis, Plataforma por la Justicia Fiscal, the Valencian tax-justice campaign, Izquierda Unida, Más Madrid, the economy minister, two Madrid politicians, an economist (2011) and Gestha's president. R004 added the 19-member Plataforma por la Justicia Fiscal (as roster claims, grade B) and its coordinator, Oxfam Intermon's report author, Greenpeace, Attac, the finance-committee spokespeople of PSOE, Sumar and PP (the PP one grade C), and Sumar's Sept 2026 bill. Searches excluded opponent outlets. R005-R006 added the Wealth Cap Project (a wealth cap is treated as a 100% levy above a threshold), its advisers and report authors, the Catalan Parlament and Comuns, EH Bildu and its Basque spokespeople, and a press roster of the parties that voted for Ley 38/2022. R007 added Navarre's parliament, the Juntas Generales de Álava, the Diputación de Gipuzkoa, the Catalan fair-taxation platform, the Finance Minister and own-site statements by CECU, Economistas sin Fronteras and Oxfam Intermon on the Tax the Rich initiative. R008 (review, 2026-10-21) loaded the 52 provinces, built the map from IGN shapes (CC BY 4.0, via es-atlas), placed deputies in their Congress constituency per Wikidata, dropped an agenda-only row for Bustinduy and moved Yago Álvarez Barba to exclusions (no wealth tax named). Municipios loaded and mapped on 2026-10-21.

polls.scope: Spain, adults with the right to vote
polls.question: A wealth tax that would apply only to people declaring assets of EUR 10 million or more (the Unidas Podemos proposal)
polls.sample: 1,078 people, telephone omnibus (about 74% on random mobile numbers), margin of error ±3.04

polls.question: An additional annual tax of 1% of total wealth on people who hold more than EUR 8 million, to fund the recovery from COVID-19
polls.commissioned_by: Millionaires for Humanity (a group of wealthy individuals who advocate a wealth tax)
polls.sample: 1,046 respondents in Spain, online (Dynata panel), part of a 10-country survey
